function_name: storage_types (RunRecord, RunStage, RunEvent, RawPayload, TagRow, EventSink, StorageError)
description: Bundled type-spec for storage's plain data-transfer dataclasses, its progress-callback protocol, and its single exception type. Grouped into one file (unlike config's dataclasses, which are each substantial cross-module contracts) because these types are simple pass-through row representations or a single-method structural protocol, with no independent validation logic of their own -- their correctness is exercised entirely through the round-trip unit tests of the read/write functions that produce and consume them. EventSink is declared here, not in orchestration, because acquisition, enrichment and analysis must not import orchestration (that would invert the Dependency Direction in ARCHITECTURE.md) -- and it is declared here rather than in a new standalone module because all three of those stage modules already depend on storage for their read/write calls, so this adds no new dependency edge.
signature:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunRecord:
    run_id: str
    started_at: datetime
    finished_at: datetime | None
    status: str
    trigger_type: str
    parent_run_id: str | None
    config: dict
    parameters_version: str
    code_version: str | None
    error_message: str | None
    notes: str | None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunStage:
    run_id: str
    stage: str
    status: str
    started_at: datetime | None
    finished_at: datetime | None
    attempt: int
    error_message: str | None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunEvent:
    event_id: int
    run_id: str
    ts: datetime
    stage: str
    level: str
    message: str
    progress: float | None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RawPayload:
    appid: int
    source: str
    fetched_at: datetime
    http_status: int
    payload: dict
    payload_sha256: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TagRow:
    appid: int
    tag: str
    votes: int | None
    rank: int | None

class EventSink(Protocol):
    def __call__(self, *, stage: str, level: str, message: str, progress: float | None = None) -> None: ...

class StorageError(Exception): ...
docstring:
Plain row-representation types shared by every storage read/write function, plus the one cross-cutting protocol every pipeline stage entry point type-hints against.

RunRecord: One row of `runs`. status is one of {'pending','running','succeeded','failed','cancelled'}; trigger_type is one of {'manual','scheduled'}. config is the deserialized config_json, which holds ONLY orchestration.PipelineConfig.to_dict() -- the run-specific choices that are not FORMULATION.md-governed (start_stage, max_catalog_pages, request_budget_override, notes). It deliberately does NOT duplicate AcquisitionConfig/EnrichmentParams/AnalysisParams: those are fully reconstructable from the separate parameters_version column plus the git-tracked config/parameters.toml at that version, so storing a second copy inside config_json would be redundant data that could drift from the source of truth. This also resolves a sequencing constraint: parameters_version (a content hash) can be computed and passed to create_run before config.load_parameters has even been called, so create_run can remain the very first preflight step (ADR: 'the run row exists before anything that can fail') without needing the parsed parameter dataclasses to exist yet.

RunStage: One row of `run_stages` (ADR-014). stage is one of {'acquisition','enrichment','analysis'}; status is drawn from the same vocabulary as RunRecord.status. A stage never attempted has no RunStage row at all -- see read_run_stages. attempt increments on every re-attempt (a resume, or a deliberate re-run after a parameter change), which is what makes repeated attempts auditable.

RunEvent: One row of `run_events`. level is one of {'debug','info','warning','error'}, matching EventSink's level vocabulary exactly, since a storage-backed EventSink implementation writes directly into this shape.

RawPayload: One row of `raw_games`. source is one of {'steamspy_all','steamspy_appdetails','steam_appdetails','steam_reviews'}. payload is the parsed JSON body; payload_sha256 is computed over the exact bytes received on the wire (before any parsing), so byte-equality of a re-fetch can be verified even if json.dumps would reorder keys.

TagRow: One row of `game_tags`. votes and rank are both optional because SteamSpy's tag payload does not guarantee vote counts for every tag; rank, when present, is the tag's position in that app's SteamSpy-reported tag ordering.

EventSink: Structural callback type for the progress/log events that orchestration passes into every stage entry point (acquisition.run_acquisition, enrichment.run_enrichment, analysis.run_analysis all type-hint their on_event parameter against this name). The concrete implementation is built by orchestration and normally wraps append_run_event; a test double is typically a simple recording lambda or list-appending closure, which satisfies the Protocol structurally with no subclassing required. A sink implementation that performs I/O must catch and locally handle its own errors, so a logging failure can never abort the pipeline stage it is reporting progress for.

StorageError: The one exception every fallible storage function raises for a storage-layer problem (schema violation, cross-thread connection misuse, unknown run_id where the contract requires an error rather than a no-op, or a finish_run_stage/begin_run_stage ordering violation). Distinguishes storage-layer failures from config.ParameterError and stage-specific errors (AcquisitionError, EnrichmentError, AnalysisError) raised by higher layers.
preconditions: RunRecord.status, RunStage.status and RunEvent.level values are always one of the CHECK-constrained sets above when constructed from a database row (the CHECK constraint guarantees this on the write path; read functions trust it on the read path)
RawPayload.payload_sha256 is lowercase hex, 64 characters (sha256 digest)
Any callable passed where EventSink is expected accepts exactly the keyword arguments stage, level, message, progress (progress optional) and returns None
postconditions: All dataclasses are frozen; storage never mutates a returned record in place
StorageError instances always carry a human-readable message; where relevant (cross-thread misuse) the message names the expected vs. actual thread id

edge_cases.input: RunRecord.finished_at read for a run still 'running'
edge_cases.expected_behavior: None, not a sentinel epoch datetime

edge_cases.input: RunStage for a stage never attempted
edge_cases.expected_behavior: no RunStage instance exists for it at all -- read_run_stages simply omits it, it is never synthesised with a placeholder status

edge_cases.input: TagRow with votes=None and rank=None (tag present but SteamSpy reported neither)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: constructed successfully; downstream code must not assume votes is always an int
not checked by the dataclass itself (it has no logic); upsert_raw_payloads is responsible for computing it correctly at write time, and its own unit tests cover the mismatch case

edge_cases.input: A plain lambda `lambda **kw: None` passed as an EventSink argument
edge_cases.expected_behavior: satisfies the Protocol structurally; no explicit subclassing or registration required

unit_tests.name: test_runrecord_roundtrip_via_get_run
unit_tests.description: Covered indirectly by create_run/get_run's own tests; this file has no standalone logic to unit test beyond field presence.

unit_tests.name: test_storageerror_message_present
unit_tests.description: StorageError('cross-thread use') stringifies to a non-empty message.

unit_tests.name: test_recording_fake_conforms_to_eventsink_protocol
unit_tests.description: A recording fake that appends (stage, level, message, progress) tuples to a list is accepted anywhere an EventSink parameter is declared (verified via static typing and a runtime call).
unit_tests.expected: call recorded with all fields preserved unchanged
